seongsu-daydrop.title:
Korean Brands to Discover
at a Seongsu Warehouse Showroom
Korean Brands to Discover at a Seongsu Warehouse Showroom
seongsu-daydrop.summary: A tour with an editor through five hidden designer brand studios in Seongsu

info.label: Meeting point
info.value: In front of Seongsu Station, Exit 4

seongsu-daydrop.intro:
Hi, I’m Editor H. Today’s Day Drop is Seongsu.
Across Seongsu, Korean brands with no store in Japan are tucked into almost every alley. They don’t show up in search, and their signs are small enough that you could walk right past them. So for half a day, let’s explore them together!

🧵 THE HARPER DAY DROP
Korean Brands to Discover at a Seongsu Warehouse Showroom

🤎 Showrooms and flagships for Korean brands you can’t buy in Japan
🤎 I’ll try things on with you and tell you honestly what suits you
🤎 Mostly shops off the main streets, the kind Seoul locals keep to themselves
🤎 ₩128,000~ (Based on 4 people)

This tour is for you if
✨ You want to buy Korean clothes but don’t know where to start
✨ You’d hesitate to walk into a shop alone
✨ You want someone to tell you whether a piece in a photo will suit you
✨ You want to keep wearing your travel finds long after you get home

What I do is simple. I pick the shops, and while you try things on, I stand beside you and say, “Buy this one, leave that one.” That way you can see in one day the places Seoul’s clothing lovers visit on weekends.

k-brand-celeb.title: Brands Made Famous by Celebrities
k-brand-celeb.summary: From celebrity picks to standout designs, nine K-brands leading today's fashion scene
k-brand-celeb.intro:
These are the brands that get the most “Where is that from?” questions in Seoul right now. From a knit that sold out in a day after a celebrity wore it, to techwear that overseas fashion insiders spotted first. They share one thing: in Seoul, you can buy them at the lowest price, get them fastest, and see them the most.

The nine brands below are the ones THE HARPER editors picked after touring showrooms in person. If something catches your eye, save it. We can stop by together on a Day Drop.

sections.heading: GLOWNY
sections.sub: Seoul-based women's wear · Strong support from women in their 20s
sections.body: This is the Seoul brand with the most loyal fan base among women in their 20s. Its signature is a sweet, vintage mood with a healthy femininity. Slim tops, knits, mini dresses, and denim, everyday pieces you reach for again and again, are its strongest items. A GLOWNY knit is basically a staple for women in Seoul.

sections.heading: OPEN YY
sections.sub: Contemporary label by sister directors · Collaborations with PUMA and KEEN
sections.body: A contemporary brand led by sisters Jiyoung and Boyoung. Among young Korean fashion fans, it’s the first name that comes up for “distinctive women’s wear.” Its experimental silhouettes move between women’s wear and unisex, and its ongoing collaborations with global brands like PUMA and KEEN keep it in the conversation every season.

sections.heading: SAN SAN GEAR
sections.sub: A rising name in gorpcore and techwear
sections.body: A next-generation brand that represents the gorpcore and techwear trend in Korea. Its outerwear and pants combine functional details with futuristic silhouettes. Wearing them doesn’t feel like “I’m in functional clothes,” but “the look is complete.” The brand is building its own utility style.

sections.heading: HYEIN SEO
sections.sub: The original Korean avant-garde streetwear label
sections.body: A designer brand that was the first to introduce Korean avant-garde streetwear to the world. Its dark, rebellious aesthetic and structured silhouettes leave a strong impression right away. It started with women's wear and now extends into men's, and overseas select shops are often the first to look for it.

sections.heading: POST ARCHIVE FACTION (PAF)
sections.body: One of the most recognized Korean contemporary brands overseas. Its core is an experimental design language that takes garments apart and reassembles them. Technical jackets and pants with asymmetric patterns and functional fabrics are its signature pieces. Try them on in Seoul and you’ll find they’re a completely different garment from what you saw in photos.

sections.heading: GROVE
sections.body: A contemporary casual brand with strong recognition among women in their 20s and 30s. The base is a clean, classic design that reinterprets 1960s vintage for today. Many of its pieces are highly versatile everyday wear like knits, tops, and skirts, which is why it's often named “the brand travelers bring home and wear the most.”

sections.heading: MATIN KIM
sections.sub: A leading K-fashion brand for Gen Z · Strong in logo accessories
sections.body: The K-fashion brand with the widest mainstream reach among Gen Z in Korea and abroad. Its core is trendy yet everyday casualwear, but its real strength is the accessory line: bags, wallets, and caps featuring its logo. Many people pick one up as a gift.

sections.heading: SINOON
sections.sub: Romantic girlish mood, with a Seoul twist
sections.body: A brand that turns romantic, girlish sensibility into a modern Seoul mood, and has quickly grown its following among women in their 20s. Its main lines are women's wear and accessories with soft silhouettes, including knits, cardigans, skirts, and dresses. The Dosan flagship is worth a visit, since the space itself is the content.

sections.heading: GENTLE MONSTER (+ Atissu)
sections.sub: A global eyewear brand that represents K-fashion
sections.body: A bold brand world that brings fashion, art, and space together around sunglasses and eyeglasses. Its experimental frame designs, large flagship stores, and steady stream of global collaborations put it in a position all its own. You can also enjoy the dessert brand Atissu in the same building.

k-brand-interview.title: K-BRAND Designer Interviews
k-brand-interview.summary: The sister directors behind two Korean brands drawing intense attention overseas
k-brand-interview.intro:
When overseas fashion people talk about “Seoul brands,” two names always come up: GLOWNY and OPEN YY. What’s interesting is that both brands are led by sisters. One handles the business, the other handles the creative side. The synergy came from different tastes and senses colliding and blending, and that’s what built the brands you see today.

In this issue, we look at how the two sister directors got started, where they are now, and how they make “the clothes we want to wear.”

sections.heading: GLOWNY Directors & Designers
sections.sub: CEO Choi Jein · Creative Director Choi Jiho
sections.body:
GLOWNY’s creative director is Choi Jiho (right in the photo). Together with her older sister, CEO Choi Jein (left), she launched GLOWNY in 2020 as a sister founding team. The roles are clear. Choi Jein oversees the whole business, while Choi Jiho takes charge of GLOWNY’s creative side, from product design to content and visuals.

“My sister reads the numbers, I look at the clothes.” That setup is the secret behind what makes GLOWNY feel so much like GLOWNY. The balance between lovely but not lightweight, and vintage but not dated, came from the two of them clashing and creating every day.

sections.heading: OPEN YY Directors & Designers
sections.sub: Sister directors Kim Jiyoung and Kim Boyoung
sections.body:
OPEN YY’s creative directors are also sisters, Kim Jiyoung and Kim Boyoung. Neither of them trained as a fashion designer. They are people who love clothes and have watched them closely for a long time. They started the brand with one wish: to make clothes they themselves would love to wear and feel excited about.

They had been running a label called THE OPEN PRODUCT, and in 2023 they renamed it OPEN YY, opening a new chapter. Today, with silhouettes that move between women's wear and unisex, it's a brand that overseas buyers seek out first.

k-brand-showroom.title: K-BRAND Showroom Guide
k-brand-showroom.summary: A one-day route through Apgujeong and Dosan, the hottest neighborhood right now, following K-brand showrooms
k-brand-showroom.intro:
Apgujeong has become Seoul’s hottest neighborhood again. Around Dosan Park especially, the showrooms of K-brands drawing attention right now sit within a 10-minute walk of each other. This route is about more than clothes. You get to experience the whole world each brand has built, from the space and music to the coffee.

Walking the stops in the order below takes about half a day. Save the map link, and if you hesitate inside a showroom, call an editor from THE HARPER.

sections.heading: House Nowhere Dosan
sections.body: The starting point of the route. It’s an editorial showroom that presents several K-brands in one space, so it's a good place to get a feel for the brands you'll see today.

sections.heading: GLOWNY Dosan
sections.body: Here you can try on the knit that sold out online in real life. If you're unsure about sizing, the staff will tell you honestly, so ask them with confidence.

sections.heading: SINOON Flagship Store Dosan
sections.body: The space itself reflects the brand’s mood. Try on the knits and dresses with soft silhouettes, and be sure to take photos while you're there.

sections.heading: ELBORN Dosan Flagship Store
sections.body: It's right next to SINOON, so it's easy to stop by next. If you're looking for simple everyday wear, you'll likely find at least one piece to take home.

sections.heading: Atelier Edition
sections.body: The first and second floors have different moods, so you'll be surprised twice. It curates Korean designer brands, which makes it a great place to find brands you've never heard of but love.

sections.heading: YUMER Dosan Branch
sections.body: A showroom that connects a basement level and the ground floor. It's good for a slow browse later in the route, and there are plenty of cafés nearby if you want a break.

sections.heading: Urbanic30
sections.body: The end of the route. The minimalist space has clothes hung sparsely, so it's a good place to sort through everything you've seen all day and pick one last piece.

0.name: Sunlove Links Seongsu
0.note: Hidden designer brand select shop in Seongsu
intro: Deep in a Seongsu alley, this select shop has a small sign that's easy to walk right past. It gathers emerging Korean designer brands, most of which have no store in Japan, so you can only buy them here.
Don't try to see everything at once. Take your time with one rack at a time. Staff tend to be honest if you're unsure about sizing, so feel free to ask them.

1.name: Point of View Seongsu
1.note: Select shop with stationery and objets
intro: There are no clothes here, but it's a good stop midway through the Seongsu tour. As you browse stationery and small objets, your shopping pace gets a short break.

2.name: LCDC SEOUL
2.note: A complex where brand shops gather
intro: Brand shops and cafés are gathered in one building. It's a good addition to the tour route on a rainy day.

3.name: ADER Space 3.0
3.note: ADER ERROR flagship, where the space itself is the attraction
intro: This is ADER ERROR's Seongsu flagship. The spatial design is as famous as the clothes, so many people come just to take photos.

4.name: BEAKER Hannam
4.note: Hannam select shop with a wide range of Korean and global brands
intro: The widest select shop in Hannam. Korean and overseas brands hang side by side, which makes them easy to compare.

5.name: AMOMENTO Hannam
5.note: Flagship for a Korean brand with no unnecessary details
intro: The flagship of a brand that makes clothes with color and line reduced to the minimum. It's the first place I recommend to anyone who wants to wear basics for a long time.

6.name: EMPTY Hannam
6.note: Select shop gathering emerging brands, run by Musinsa
intro: An offline select shop run by Musinsa. You can try on in person the emerging brands you've only seen online.

A brand led by sisters, started in 2020.
